newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lenin's body to receive latest makeover.
newsitem.headline: Lenin's body to receive latest makeover.

text.p: Vladimir Lenin, the Soviet leader whose body is still on public display in Red Square 73 years after his death, is scheduled to undergo his latest makeover later this month, officials said on Friday.
Since Lenin's death in 1924, Lenin's mausoleum has closed for several months every year and a half or so to enable embalmers to give the body a thorough refreshening.
Mausoleum duty officer Mikhail Moravyov said on Friday that the mausoleum would close from January 27 to March 24. He said that the usual "repairs" would take place during this time.
Under the once secret technique revealed by former embalmers after the fall of Communism, scientists use such periods to immerse Lenin's body in a tub of chemicals for several months to hydrate it.
Although no longer the must-see attraction it was under communism, Lenin's mausoleum remains open to the public five days a week for three hours a day.
